newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela says he won't bow to S.African unions.
newsitem.headline: Mandela says he won't bow to S.African unions.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela said in remarks broadcast on Monday that his government would not necessarily bow to the demands of trade unions in alliance with his African National Congress.

"I'm perfectly firm about it, that there are cases where the government will say 'we do not agree with you, we're going on'," Mandela said in an interview with the South African Broadcasting Corporation.

He was responding to a question about the objections of the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) to aspects of the government's Growth, Employment and Redistribution programme including plans to create a more flexible labour market.
Cosatu has demanded that planned employment legislation should provide for a 40-hour work week within five years and six months maternity leave with four months being paid.
A proposed law currently under debate proposes a 45-hour week and an increase in annual paid leave from two to three weeks a year and maternity leave of four months.

"We are not looking at the interests just of a section such as labour. We are looking at the interests of everybody in the country, workers and otherwise, and for that reason we will take a decision sometimes even though the workers are against it," Mandela said.

The ANC, Cosatu and the South African Communist Party held talks earlier this month in a bid to resolve their differences on economic policy but said afterwards problems remained. They are due to hold another meeting in June.
